findings.origin: One Linux full-matrix failed assertion, subsequently independently reproduced with controlled actual React interaction.
findings.failure: The second commit preview after hiding/returning never displayed its confirmation checkbox; the final DOM had an enabled inspect control, no active reading state and no error.
findings.cause: Git status completion publishes enabled=true. A click can start inspect and assign controller.current before the previous passive effect cleanup/setup runs. That old cleanup aborts the new controller and the setup clears preview/reading. Waiting for disabled=false already existed and does not establish that passive lifecycle work is complete.

reproduction.source: 256 exact frozen web/shared copies, retained with manifest
reproduction.trace: clicked:true; returned automatic status/diff/refs not aborted; first-enabled-click emits exactly one new workspace/git/status with signal.aborted:true, no subsequent staged diff or final status, and no checkbox.
reproduction.limits: This controlled reproduction proves the reachable defect. The original full matrix did not record its precise request/effect scheduling, so the report does not assert an identical observed microtask trace there.

findings.repair: Move only the [visible,enabled,epoch] invalidation effect to useLayoutEffect. Cleanup and state reset finish in commit before the new DOM control can be used. Retain render-time activity/owner keys, abort checks after every await, drafts, the separate not_sent effect, and durable receipt semantics.

findings.origin: Narrow analogous-consumer investigation, not another full-matrix failed assertion.
findings.cause: The same-key project/source lifecycle cleanup reads mutable pending.current after a new request may start. Initial passive setup can also clear a synchronously decoded inline preview after its first button publication.

reproduction.limits: Actual createRoot and single MutationObserver-triggered DOM clicks; APIs and object-URL endpoints are isolated fixture boundaries. No hook mock, sleep, repeated click or network/media provider request.

findings.repair: Move the media source lifecycle effect to useLayoutEffect. Preserve the existing abort ownership checks, source verification, image budgets, URL release and generated-media reservation release.

preservedCoverage: All nine original Git draft tests remain unchanged, including the original failing full-matrix case. They retain hide/hidden-handler gating, late response rejection, draft survival, owner ABA reset, unknown receipt ownership and no repeated commit.

Two added Git regressions exercise first-enabled actual DOM single click with exact status/diff/status and nonaborted signals, plus disabled preview cancellation, blocked disabled handlers and late result rejection.

Both added media regressions use actual first-publication clicks, assert the image persists, assert exact API/URL ownership and release URLs exactly once on unmount. Existing attachment/generated/MCP media boundaries remain in targeted verification.
No test timeout, worker count, retry, expected behavior or protection was weakened. No change to backend requests, formats, commit semantics or media storage.
selectionBoundary: The actual eight-module selection includes git-index-ui, not modal-mutations. modal-mutations imports WorkspacePanel but exercises its files-tab mkdir/copy/remove routes without activating Git or mounting WorkspaceCommit, and does not consume MessageMedia. Import matching alone does not establish execution of the changed effects. No targeted execution of modal-mutations is claimed.

observations: Conversation cleanup binds a local AbortController and its visit invalidation is layout-bound; its mutable-ref invalidate is a synchronous event, not old passive cleanup. EmergencyRecovery already uses layout; ReceiptMaintenance cleanup is unmount-only.
The other workspace previews do not use this mutable-controller passive cleanup mechanism. No unproved broad lifecycle rewrite was introduced.
MessageMedia was not changed based on text similarity: the unloaded same-key project transition and initial inline publication each failed in the isolated old-code probe before repair.

whyPreviousVerificationMissedIt: Earlier static review verified invalidation on hiding/owner changes but did not account for newly interactive DOM being published before passive cleanup.

The ordinary Testing Library interaction tests wait for enabled controls and usually flush effects before the next click. Passing previous full matrices or targeted reruns did not cover the first-publication interleaving.
The original matrix failure was not dismissed as flakiness or repaired by another wait; its consumer path was traced and a controlled real React ordering regression now preserves the defect scenario.
prevention: For callbacks created by first-mounted or newly enabled controls, verify lifecycle cleanup and reset occur before those controls are interactive, not merely before the next ordinary test click. Pair exact first-publication requests with old-owner cancellation, draft preservation and resource-release assertions; preserve failures and use controlled event ordering instead of retries or timing changes.

linux.identity: ordinary UID65534 isolated runtime-targeted; immutable candidates and original reproduction directory not modified

verification.actualTestsThisRepair: Initial Git/workspace80 and media68 runs are preserved as intermediate checks. After the final media change, reran all eight related modules together on each platform against final source because WorkspaceCommit imports Messages, which consumes MessageMedia. The final complete 148-case sets and source hashes, not the earlier split runs, establish this targeted verification.

diagnosticLimitations: The first Linux Git probe executed zero tests because its default Vitest cache path was not writable. Its failed environment log is preserved; only the diagnostic cache path changed before the single effective original-code reproduction. It is not counted as a product assertion failure.

A preliminary Windows media probe first recorded one missing-image failure; the expanded diagnostic then recorded both distinct media traces. These are separate diagnostic executions, not multiple full-matrix failures.
No complete matrix or hosted CI was run after this repair; a clean new exact-source audit and authorized full matrix remain mandatory. Original matrix3 remains failed.
